plan: Final design document delivered in 11 numbered sections. (1) Objective and hypotheses with two-arm co-equal framing and explicit both-or-partial saturation rule (Note 1). (2) Variables and factors table. (3) Models (Vicuna-7B-v1.5, Llama-2-7B-chat, Llama-3-1-8B-Instruct) and attack-family rationale (GCG primary, BEAST secondary, AutoDAN out of scope). (4) Suffix-length sweep {0,1,2,5,10,20,50,100,200,500} with committed per-L optimization budgets 500 for L in {1..20}, 2500 for L in {50,100}, and 5000 for L in {200,500} (Note 3) plus a rejection-based truncation policy. (5) Judge = Llama-Guard-3-8B primary, Llama-Guard-2-8B fallback (separate 8B model loaded only at eval, never in the optimization loop) and per-behavior plus per-attempt ASR definitions. (6) Arms A trained-at-evaluated-at, B prefix-of-suffix at L*=500, C BEAST secondary, D tokenizer robustness at L in {0,50,500} on Llama-2-7B-chat under GPT-2 BPE (Note 4 scope). (7) Composite saturation criterion (Note 2): marginal-gain with tau=0.02 over two consecutive doublings plus bootstrap CI on Delta includes zero AND (broken-stick with CI-width <= 0.5 * L_lower_bound OR sigmoid fit with L_50 reported); plus the explicit three-number summary card (Note 5) with verbal call. (8) External-compute cap (Note 6) with per-arm table <=24/8/8/4 GPU-hr per model on A100 for Arms A/B/C/D, judge cost acknowledged as separate <=6 GPU-hr/model absorbed into the cap, total <=48/model primary plus <=48/model secondary combined, plus itemized cost note for additional L values. (9) Literature-anchored forecast (Zou 2023, Andriushchenko 2024, Sadasivan 2024, Mazeika 2024, Chao 2024) with direction and L* range tables, explicitly flagged as forecasts not measurements. (10) Threats to validity matrix including judge-version variance, optimization stochasticity, tokenizer compression, behavior-set composition, decoding, capability/white-box assumption, and estimator disagreement. (11) Limitations of a design-only deliverable: no measurements produced; external compute, weights, and judge hosting required; forecasts may be miscalibrated; defenses out of primary scope. All six researcher notes incorporated by name.

context.question: How does the **length of adversarial suffix** used in token-level jailbreak attacks affect the **Attack Success Rate (ASR)** of LLMs? Specifically, is there a saturation point beyond which longer suffixes no longer improve attack effectiveness?
context.context: Design an experiment that answers the question. The researcher can clarify source-supported setup details by topic. Do not claim that an experiment was run.
